findings.title: Stats page shows a failed request as "No harvests in this range" with no error and no retry
findings.steps: Sign in. Open /stats while the API is failing or unreachable (or trigger any 4xx/5xx, e.g. /stats?from=2026-05-01&to=2026-01-01).
findings.expected: An error message that the stats could not be loaded, with a Retry button. Other pages do this, e.g. the dashboard's AlertMessage on summaryError.
findings.actual: The page never reads `error` from useApiFetch. Any failure lands in the v-else-if branch and shows the empty state "No harvests in this range – Pick a different date range, or log a harvest". There is no retry other than changing the dates.
findings.evidence: Server-side render of /stats?from=2026-05-01&to=2026-01-01 contains "No harvests in this range". The API answered 422 {"detail":"The From date must be on or before the To date."}. The code destructures only { data, status } and has no error branch.

findings.title: Invalid date range (From after To) is shown as an empty result instead of the server's validation message
findings.steps: On /stats, type a From date later than the To date (the min/max attributes do not stop typed or URL values), e.g. /stats?from=2026-05-01&to=2026-01-01.
findings.expected: A visible reason, such as "The From date must be on or before the To date."
findings.actual: "No harvests in this range". It looks like there really are no harvests, and the 422 detail is thrown away.
findings.evidence: Observed in the SSR HTML. The API returns a 422 with the detail string.

findings.title: Impossible date in the URL (e.g. 2026-02-30) is shown as an empty range
findings.steps: Open /stats?from=2026-02-30. It passes the page's /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ check and is sent to the API.
findings.expected: Fall back to the default date, or show a validation error.
findings.actual: The API answers 422 and the page shows "No harvests in this range".
findings.evidence: SSR HTML for /stats?from=2026-02-30 contains "No harvests in this range". The API returns 422 date_from_datetime_parsing.

findings.title: Stats request has no 10 s timeout, so a hung API leaves "Loading stats…" up indefinitely
findings.steps: Make the API accept the connection but never respond, then open or refresh /stats.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 seconds and an error with a retry is shown.
findings.actual: No timeout is set in useApiFetch/useApiClient or in the page. The page stays on "Loading stats…", and once it does fail it shows the empty state (see the first finding).
findings.evidence: Code reading: grep finds no timeout anywhere in frontend/app.

findings.title: After a failed refetch, stale data or the empty state can be shown for the newly chosen range
findings.steps: Load a valid range, then change the dates so that the request fails (server down or invalid range).
findings.expected: An error tied to the new range.
findings.actual: Nothing tells the user the request failed. Depending on how Nuxt handles data on error, the page shows either the old range's table and range text ("N harvests from <old dates>") or a false empty state, while the inputs show the new dates.
findings.evidence: Code reading: there is no error handling, and rangeText/table render whenever stats.value is truthy.
